paragraphs.text: Thariq Shihipar, an engineer on Anthropic's Claude Code team, announced on October 24, 2026, that he has left the company after more than a year working on the coding tool, according to TokenPost and Mezha. He shared the news in a post on X under his handle @trq212.

In the post, Shihipar wrote that he had "left Anthropic after more than a year of working on Claude Code and seeing it scale larger than I ever imagined." He added that he had loved working at the company and believed deeply in its mission, singling out the idea of a race to the top among AI developers.

Shihipar did not give a reason for the move and did not name a new employer. Both TokenPost and Mezha reported that he plans to take a break before starting something new. He described the job as the most enjoyable of his career, and at times the most stressful, and said he trusted his colleagues to keep leading the work.

He also pointed his followers to other people working on Claude Code for future updates, naming Boris Cherny, Cat Wu, Addy Osmani and Lydia Hallie, as well as Anthropic's @ClaudeDevs account. Mezha reported that Hallie replied publicly, saying working with him had been inspiring and wishing him well.
A public face for Claude Code

Shihipar was one of the most visible people behind the product. TokenPost noted that he regularly shared Claude Code features and usage tips on X. The Latent Space podcast, which interviewed him in an episode titled "Claude Code's Next Era," described him as the explainer of the team and said much of his time went to teaching people how to use the tool, alongside engineering work that fed user feedback back into the product.

Latent Space said he has a background in human computer interaction, worked on Anthropic's Agent SDK earlier, and contributed to features including Ask User Question, artifacts, Claude Tag, Projects and Claude Mods. Before Anthropic, according to Mezha, he was engineering director of PubPub, a project associated with the MIT Media Lab, and cofounded One More Multiverse, a tabletop role playing game platform that went through Y Combinator.

The announcement drew a wide response on X. A Digg roundup of the story collected replies from well-known figures in the AI community, many of them congratulating him on his run. AI researcher Yuchen Jin joked that "He quit because he can finally afford the Opus bill," a reference to the cost of Anthropic's top model. Other posts in the roundup tied the timing to Anthropic's plans to go public.

For most users, a single engineer leaving does not change how Claude Code works on any given day. Shihipar's exit stands out because so much of the tool's public explanation ran through his account, which made the loss partly one of communication rather than code. His decision to name other team members on his way out reads as an effort to hand that role on. The timing also draws attention, because coverage of the departure linked it to Anthropic's expected public listing, a period when the movements of well-known product people tend to get extra scrutiny.

The next thing to watch is where Shihipar lands after his break, and whether the colleagues he named, along with the @ClaudeDevs account, take over the steady stream of feature walkthroughs that many Claude Code users relied on.
